name: Into the Flood Maw
oracle_text:
Gift a tapped Fish (You may promise an opponent a gift as you cast this spell. If you do, they create a tapped 1/1 blue Fish creature token before its other effects.)
Return target creature an opponent controls to its owner's hand. If the gift was promised, instead return target nonland permanent an opponent controls to its owner's hand.
blocked_sentences: Return target creature an opponent controls to its owner's hand. If the gift was promised, instead return target nonland permanent an opponent controls to its owner's hand.

needs.what: a way for a card's own target spec to be declared only under a particular cast-time variant, so one printed target word can have two different selectors -- e.g. a `variant` field on a TargetModel/TargetSpec taking a cast-choice name ("gift_promised", "unpromised", "kicked", "unkicked", "overloaded"), parallel to the existing `mode` field, plus target enumeration in `legality._cast_options` that builds a separate tuple set per variant from the specs that variant activates. Into the Flood Maw needs exactly one target either way: `{types: ["Creature"], controller: "opponent"}` when unpromised and `{not_types: ["Land"], controller: "opponent"}` when the gift was promised, with legality, fizzling and the resolution-time `return_to_hand` all reading whichever one was declared
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `legality._cast_options` (src/commanderblitz/engine/legality.py:701) computes `tuples = enumerate_target_tuples(state, pid, card.targets, ...)` **once**, before any variant exists, and hands the identical tuple list to every `_cast_variant` call -- unkicked and kicked, unpromised and each gift promisee. So the promise cannot widen or narrow what the spell may point at; `gift_to` only rides along on the Action. `TargetModel`/`TargetSpec` carry no condition of any kind: `selector` clauses (`selector_keys`) are evaluated against one candidate object in isolation and none of them can ask about the cast, and `gift_promised`/`kicked` live in `condition_keys`, which only an `if` op may read at resolution -- far too late, since the target was locked in at 601.2c. The nearest existing thing is `mode`, which does gate a spec on a cast-time choice, but it is the wrong choice and is refused here twice: `loader._compile_targets` accepts `mode` only on a card whose whole effect tree is a single top-level `choose_mode`, and a mode is a free player election, not the gift promise -- writing the two lines as modes would let a player take the wide nonland-permanent bounce without ever promising the Fish. `bestow` is the one variant that does change what a spell points at, but its list is the fixed rules constant `BESTOW_TARGET` (carddef.py), not a per-variant selector a card may write. The workaround of declaring two specs (t1 creature, t2 nonland permanent) and branching with `if {gift_promised: ...}` at resolution is not the card: both specs would have to be legal and locked at cast time, so an unpromised cast would still require and announce a nonland-permanent target and a promised cast would still require a creature -- two target words where the card prints one, changing legality, what opponents can respond to, and when the spell fizzles. `optional: true` on the second spec does not save it either: it makes the extra target the caster's free choice rather than the promise's consequence. The first printed line, "Gift a tapped Fish", is fully expressible (`gift: "a tapped Fish"` plus a `create_token` of `fish_1_1_u`, tapped, `controller: "gift_recipient"`, exactly as parting_gust writes it), so only the second line is blocked and no partial answer was written.
